subject: Request: forensic artifacts and temporary access scope during high-latency outage
messages:
From: Tom Holden <tom.holden@fastfin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-04T22:18:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden latency spike + auditor request for traces

Soojin —

We saw a huge latency spike across our production token streams last night (approx 23:10-23:50 PDT). Our ops team captured customer-facing errors and has asked for the following so we can share with our internal auditors tomorrow:

- Per-request runtime traces (full request/response, timestamps, and any kernel-level errors) for the window 2028-03-04T23:05:00Z to 2028-03-04T23:55:00Z
- KV-cache hit/miss samples for affected requests
- Any tokenization mismatches or decoder errors reported by the runtime

We need to know: can Redwood provide these artifacts within 24 hours? Also, what redaction or PII-handling will you perform before sharing? Our auditors require chain-of-custody notes and a short executive summary for the incident (latency, error-rate bump, throughput dip).

Thanks — Tom
Tom Holden
Head of Ops, FastFin
[Attachment: fastfin-error-sample.json (42 KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Holden <tom.holden@fastfin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-04T23:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike + auditor request for traces

Tom —

Thanks for flagging this and for the sample. We're on it. Short answers up front:

- Yes, we can produce runtime traces and a KV-cache sample for that window within 24 hours.
- We will apply our standard incident sanitization: redact direct PII, hash user identifiers, and provide a manifest describing redaction steps.
- For chain-of-custody, we'll include export checksums, who accessed artifacts, and an S3 presigned ephemeral link with audit logging.

I've looped in Marcus (runtime) and Steph (security/compliance) to confirm scope and access model. Marcus — can your team package NDJSON traces and a small KV sample and drop them to a controlled Drive link? Steph — any additional restrictions from legal/retention side we should enforce before handing artifacts to FastFin or Allowing auditor access?

I'll coordinate exec summary and a short timeline for Tom's auditors.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: incident-ops-timelines-template.docx (18 KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Tom Holden <tom.holden@fastfin.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-05T01:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike + auditor request for traces

Soojin / Tom —

We pulled the runtime traces for the requested UTC window and sampled the KV-cache events correlated to the error signatures Tom shared. Plan:

- Produce a trimmed NDJSON export (runtime-trace-2028-03-04.ndjson) with one line per request containing timestamps, model variant, node id, latency_ms, error_code (if any), and an event trace array.
- KV-cache-sample-03-04.txt will include hashed keys and hit/miss flags + small payload sizes.
- We will NOT include full request payloads with customer-generated text; instead we will include token counts and hashed request IDs so your auditors can correlate without seeing raw prompts.

Access and packaging:
- Artifacts will be uploaded to a limited-access Drive folder and an S3 bucket with object-level audit logging enabled.
- For external auditor access, we can issue time-limited, scope-limited credentials (pre-signed S3 URLs or a short-lived GDrive share).
- I will compute SHA256 checksums for all files and include a manifest (manifest-FF-2345.json).

ETA: first package ready for internal review by 2028-03-05T08:30:00-07:00, then we'll hand off to security for redaction checks.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
[Attachment: manifest-FF-2345.json (2 KB)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Tom Holden <tom.holden@fastfin.com>
Date: 2028-03-05T07:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike + auditor request for traces

Tom / team —

Thanks Marcus — that's the right approach. A few security controls we will enforce before any external handoff:

1) Redaction policy: any token sequences that match email addresses, SSNs, or long numeric sequences will be redacted. We'll keep hashed identifiers for correlation (salted SHA256 with per-export salt recorded in the manifest).
2) Minimal access: auditors will receive pre-signed archives with a 48-hour expiry. We will not create long-lived credentials.
3) Legal hold: because FastFin's auditors requested artifacts, Legal asked we record the request as a limited legal hold for 30 days; retention policy remains: production logs are retained 90 days by default, but this exported package will be recorded separately with access logs.
4) Chain-of-custody: manifest includes who created, who reviewed (security), checksum, and a short note explaining redaction heuristics.

I will review the NDJSON for any residual sensitive sequences and sign off. Please include an internal reviewer from FastFin (ops or sec) on the Drive share so we capture the acceptance ack.

— Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redaction-spec-2028.pdf (12 KB)]

From: Tom Holden <tom.holden@fastfin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@auditco.com>, ops@fastfin.com, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-05T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike + auditor request for traces

Appreciate the rapid turnaround and the clear controls. Two quick asks before you hand off:

1) Exec summary: could Redwood provide a one-page executive summary that captures root-cause hypothesis, impact (requests/minute and error-rate delta), and mitigation steps taken? Our CISO will want that for our postmortem.
2) SLA credit: we may open a formal SLA credit request after our internal postmortem — any guidance on the expected timeline for Redwood review and decisioning?

We'll wait for the package and manifest. Please include the Drive link and the acceptance acknowledgement flow for our auditor.

Thanks all — Tom
Tom Holden
Head of Ops, FastFin
[Attachment: fastfin-ci-sample.log (8 KB)]
